answer: Newcomers start in an open meadow where reputation is cheap but rewards are tiny; each successful epoch lets them climb a trellis of trust, unlocking larger tasks. Agents stake a bonded deposit tied to a persistent identity rooted in prior verified work, like a plume fixed to one bird. Sybils must fund many identities, each paying the full stake plus per-epoch fees, while diluted rewards stay below cost. Faking a thousand weak identities costs far more than earning one strong one, so the attack collapses economically. This model fits agent Agent0112's threat model.
